title: Roadblock Detection Fix Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · parent issue #587 · designs approved 2026-11-23, with the audit
approval: Build plan approved: roadblock detection fix

short.lead: The fix is built in four steps under parent issue #587: detection, a record check, two model layers, then never waiting in unattended or bypass mode. Check my readings of your answers in the first card, because three are my interpretation.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: Always flagged: nine inability phrases. Stall phrases (not done, I've stopped, I've stopped here, next step) are checked only at the end of the turn, in unattended or bypass mode, and then a goal check decides. The goal check may block up to 6 times in a row. A first try never counts; three failed attempts by different methods are listed.
Tell me if a reading is wrong.

items.caption: My readings: the 6-block limit, the end-of-turn timing and the mode gate.

items: Matches both apostrophes, ignores quoted lines, adds the nine phrases and the four stall phrases, reads the permission mode, ignores system messages that are not yours, reads only the end of the transcript, and makes the check really block twice.

items.caption: Step 1 changes the claim pattern and the counter.

items: A claim passes only after three failed attempts in three kinds of method, all about one target, from any tool. The reply lists them. A reply marking NEEDS YOU for a licence, login, purchase or destructive step is exempt.

items.caption: Three existence checks count as one kind.

items: #591: the model judge and the goal check

A small model judges every reply at turn end. When a stall phrase appears, a second check reads the session goal and decides whether work can carry on. Each model call costs about $0.002. Both layers fail open and say so.

items.caption: Measured on three made-up sessions: all three verdicts were right.

items: #590: never wait, docs, version, QA page

In unattended or bypass mode I choose a reversible design and carry on. This adds one rule sentence and extends the no-questions hook to bypass mode. I also update the docs and version, and post a QA page after testing it myself.
Nothing from you until the QA page.

items.caption: This rule applies only in unattended and bypass mode.

changes: scripts/house_rules/core.py: claim pattern, counter and turn window
Step 1 widens detection and fixes the block count.

Done when: new verify.py test cases pass for each phrase with both apostrophes, a quoted claim is ignored, stall phrases are scanned only when unattended or bypass, and a retry is blocked a second time but never a third.
Step 2 replaces the probe test with three related failed attempts.

Done when: a claim after only git ls-files is blocked, one after three failed attempts in three kinds of method that are all named in the reply is accepted, and a failed PowerShell or other-server tool call counts as an attempt.
hooks/hooks.json and a nested goal check
Step 3 adds the judge hook and the goal check.

Done when: a stall phrase with the goal reached passes, one with the goal unreached blocks with the judge's reason, a missing or failing claude program is announced and never blocks, and the judge hook is listed in hooks.json.
show-dont-tell.md, the no-questions hook, docs and version
Step 4 stops waiting in unattended and bypass mode.

Done when: an unattended session that ends with next step and an unreached goal is blocked and carries on, a bypass-mode design question is denied with the choose-and-carry-on reason, and the injected rules stay under 9,700 characters at a runner-like path.
